headline: Record quarter as investment banking surges, margins widen
summary_short: Stifel's Q2 2026 net revenues rose 13.0% y/y to $1.45 billion, the best second quarter in company history, as diluted EPS climbed 50.6% y/y to $1.34 on a 42.2% surge in investment banking revenue.
summary_long: Investment banking revenue rose 42% y/y (advisory +24%, equity capital raising +121%, fixed-income capital raising +18%), while Global Wealth Management net revenue grew 13% on higher transactional, asset management, and net-interest income. GAAP pre-tax margin expanded to 20.6% from 16.6% as 13.0% net revenue growth outpaced a 7.6% rise in expenses; the compensation ratio fell to 57.4% from 60.3%. The company repurchased $177.0 million of stock (2.4 million shares) and declared a $0.34/share dividend, unchanged sequentially. Tangible book value per share rose 15.0% y/y to $25.52; cash rose 18% y/y to $2.19 billion. No forward guidance was issued in this release.

drivers.explanation: Best second-quarter net revenues in company history, driven by higher investment banking, asset management, and commission revenues plus net interest income; management cited a record first half.
Advisory revenue +24% on higher completed deal volume; equity capital raising +121% on higher volumes and larger deal sizes; fixed-income capital raising +18% on higher bond issuance.
Growth driven by higher investment banking, asset management, and commission revenues, plus net interest income, per the release's own highlights.
Net revenue grew 13.0% y/y while total non-interest expenses grew only 7.6%, expanding GAAP pre-tax margin to 20.6% from 16.6%.
EPS growth outpaced net income growth partly because weighted average diluted shares fell 1.0% y/y on continued share buybacks.
Decrease was primarily due to share repurchases, per the company's own disclosure.
